sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Preble County, Ohio?
sections.html:
Deeds and mortgages are recorded at the Preble County Recorder's office on the second floor of the courthouse at 101 E. Main Street, Eaton, OH 45320. The phone is (937) 456-8173. According to the recorder's page, the office keeps hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, but the courthouse front door is locked at 4:00 p.m., so plan to arrive before then.

Eaton is the county seat. Wikipedia says Preble County was formed on February 15, 1808, from parts of Butler and Montgomery Counties, and it covers 426 square miles with a 2020 population of 40,999. About three in four residents live in rural areas.

Check with the office about holiday hours before you plan a trip around a closing date.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Preble County?
sections.html:
The county's printed schedule is simple. Recording and indexing a deed, mortgage, affidavit, easement, land contract, lease, mechanic's lien, trust or power of attorney costs $39.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each page after that. Each marginal notation is $4.00.

  • A certified copy runs $2.00 a page, plus $1.00 for each seal.
  • A document that misses Ohio's standardization rules in R.C. 317.114 costs $20.00 more.
  • Court, tax authority, state and federal documents, plats and DD 214 discharges are exempt from that $20.00, as are papers signed before July 1, 2009.
  • Filing a military discharge, or getting a photocopy of one, is free.

The state fee statute, R.C. 317.32, builds the first-two-page amount from a $17 base fee, a $17 housing trust fund fee and an optional preservation charge of up to $5, which is how a county reaches a figure like $39. Include a self-addressed stamped envelope with adequate postage if you want the recorded document mailed back to you.

sections.h2: How should a Preble County deed be formatted?
sections.html:
Preble County's page lists the formatting rules in detail, and following them avoids the surcharge. Documents go on white 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inch paper, in black or blue ink, in a font of at least 10 point. They must be originals, not photocopies, with no highlighting or white-out.

  • Leave a 3-inch margin at the top of the first page, which is reserved for the recorder, auditor and engineer stamps.
  • Leave 1.5 inches at the top of every later page and at least 1 inch on the sides and bottom.
  • Print the name of the person who prepared the document, and print or type names under hard-to-read signatures.
  • State the grantor's marital status, and give the grantee's tax mailing address.
  • Include a full legal description and prior recording information, approved by the engineer before recording.

The grantor signs and acknowledges the deed before a notary public. The conveyance document must also carry the stamps of the county engineer and county auditor showing the grantor complied with R.C. 319.202.

sections.h2: What does the Preble County auditor charge on a sale?
sections.html:
The recorder's page states that the auditor's conveyance fee is $3.00 per $1,000 of the selling price, and the transfer fee is 50 cents per parcel. Those are collected at the auditor's counter, which is on the second floor of the same courthouse at (937) 456-8148, before the deed is taken upstairs or down the hall to be recorded.

Ohio law also lets a county commission levy a real property transfer tax, capped at 30 cents per $100 of value, under R.C. 322.02. The grantor pays any such tax to the auditor before recording. Ask the auditor whether Preble County has one before you total your net proceeds.

The county's Office of Land Use Management, at 937-456-8171 on the first floor, answers questions about property splits and building permits. A lot split matters if you are selling part of a parcel, because the legal description has to be right before the engineer will approve it.

sections.h2: Which Preble County offices handle a home sale?
sections.html:
All three main offices share the courthouse, so a seller can finish most of the errands in one trip.

Preble County courthouse offices for a home sale, with phone numbers as printed on the county's own pages
OfficeUsed forPhone
RecorderRecording deeds, mortgages and releases(937) 456-8173
AuditorConveyance fee, transfer, valuation complaints(937) 456-8148
TreasurerPaying property tax(937) 456-8140

The county FAQ confirms that the treasurer's office is on the courthouse's second floor and takes property tax payments. The sheriff's office handles sheriff's sales on Fridays at 9 a.m. in the first-floor lobby of the courthouse, which is where a foreclosure sale of a Preble County home would be held.

sections.h2: How do I search Preble County land records?
sections.html:
The recorder offers an online search index, a title fraud service and a fraud sleuth profile through its page. The county's note on its records says indexes available online start December 14, 1999, through a CountyFusion site, and the Ohio Recorders Association page for Preble County links to the same system. For older deeds, you need to visit the office or ask staff.

The same page describes the recorder's purpose as a complete, accurate and permanent record of documents that convey or burden land, used by attorneys, historians, genealogists and land title examiners. If you are tracing an old farm or a family transfer, ask for the volume and page once you find the entry in the index.

Owners who are worried about forged deeds can register for the free title fraud service the page links.

sections.h2: Can the Preble County Board of Revision change my value before I sell?
sections.html:
It can lower or raise a value, but only through a complaint filed in the right window. The auditor's Board of Revision page says the Board accepts a DTE Form 1 complaint from January 1 through March 31 of the following tax year, and it has to reach the auditor's office by 4:30 p.m. on March 31. A mailed complaint counts if postmarked on or before the deadline.

The Board's members are the county auditor, the county treasurer and a county commissioner or representative, and the page cites R.C. 5715.13 through 5715.19 as the source of its authority. Questions go to (937) 456-8197 or (937) 456-8131. A late or defective complaint may be dismissed without a hearing, so file early.

sections.h2: Where do other Preble County matters go besides the recorder?
sections.html:
A sale sometimes pulls in other offices, and the county's FAQ sorts out who handles what. Evictions and small claims are heard by the Eaton Municipal Court at 1199 Preble Drive, phone 937-456-4941. Probate Court on the second floor of the courthouse, at 937-456-8137, takes name changes and estates cases, which matters if the house passed to heirs. The Clerk of Courts is on the third floor at 937-456-8160.

Sheriff's sales run on Fridays beginning at 9 a.m. in the first-floor lobby, and the sheriff's office at 937-456-6262 has details. A seller facing one of those sales or a tenant dispute can still deal with the recorder and auditor in the usual order, but should line up the court side first.

faqs.q: How much does the Preble County recorder charge for a deed?
faqs.a: The county prints $39.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each additional page. A marginal notation adds $4.00, and a nonconforming document adds $20.00.

faqs.q: What is the Preble County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The county's recorder page lists $3.00 per $1,000 of the selling price plus 50 cents per parcel, paid to the auditor before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: What time does the Preble County recorder's office close?
faqs.a: The office is open until 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, but the courthouse front door is locked at 4:00 p.m. Arrive before 4:00, or call (937) 456-8173 if you are running late.

faqs.q: Can I get my DD 214 from the Preble County recorder?
faqs.a: Yes. Military discharge papers are kept at the recorder's office, and filing a discharge or getting a photocopy of it carries no fee.

faqs.q: When does the Preble County Board of Revision take complaints?
faqs.a: From January 1 through March 31 of the year after the tax year in question, with a 4:30 p.m. cutoff on March 31 at the auditor's office. Mailed complaints must be postmarked by that date.
